fable.w: This section consists entirely of technical conforming amendments that replace references to the Bank Insurance Fund and Savings Association Insurance Fund with "Deposit Insurance Fund" across several banking statutes, plus an effective date. The tempting reading is that words like "member" or the heading "Investments Promoting Public Welfare" signal outside involvement, but these are only statutory terms being edited. Nothing provides for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to various federal statutes, primarily replacing references to former insurance funds (SAIF, BIF) with the unified Deposit Insurance Fund. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. The changes are purely administrative and definitional within the federal legal framework.
qwen_block.s: The paragraph designated the “Eleventh” of section 5136 of the Revised Statutes of the United States (12 U.S.C. 24) is amended in the 5th sentence, by striking “affected deposit insurance fund” and inserting “Deposit Insurance Fund”.

opus.w: This section only makes technical conforming amendments, replacing references to the Bank Insurance Fund and Savings Association Insurance Fund with "Deposit Insurance Fund" across several banking statutes, effective when the funds merge. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory committee or right to sue. The many statute names and federal bodies make it look procedural, but nothing in it brings outsiders into a decision.
opus.b:
This section makes **no** provision for participation.

1. **The tempting reading:** It names many statutes and federal bodies (the Federal Reserve Act, the Federal Home Loan Bank Act, the Deposit Insurance Fund). That procedural-sounding framing might look like a federal decision process. It isn't one. These are technical conforming amendments that swap old fund names for "Deposit Insurance Fund" when the two insurance funds merge. No outside party is consulted, there is no hearing, no comment period or rulemaking, no advisory body, and no right to sue.
